observed: Before fix/cf-stream-parts, a part upload read its 8-64 MiB body into JS: 61-359 ms CPU per part; after a burst Cloudflare killed them (exceededCpu, error 1102, HTTP 503). A 1 GB upload to R2 never completed (6 sessions). After the fix a part PUT takes 3-9 ms CPU (256 MB run) and 1 GiB uploads complete in one session (2026-11-02 runs).
carton: Before: a clear HTTP error, 4 retries with backoff, then a resumable stop that never finished. Fixed by streaming the part body to R2 or the vault (fix/cf-stream-parts).

observed: A 96 MiB part failed 503 while another upload shared the isolate; a 99 MiB part alone passed.
carton: Same retry path; streaming parts (fix/cf-stream-parts) no longer buffers them.

value: 100 MB request body (Free and Pro plans)
observed: A 101 MiB part: 413 at the edge; 64, 96 and 99 MiB passed.
carton: Client parts are 8 MiB by default and at most 64 MiB unless a file passes 640 GiB (10,000 parts).

observed: A raw 33 MiB frame: Cloudflare closes 1009; the room closes 1009 above its own 24 MiB cap.
carton: Changes over 1 MiB go as envelopes through blob storage (5 MiB: 2.0-3.5 s, 20 MiB: 3.9-5.1 s, both hosts); a 30 MiB change is refused locally as too large in 215 ms and the next edit still confirms.

value: 1,000 internal subrequests per request (R2 binding calls; Workers Free), 50 external
observed: blobs/heads with 200 keys ok (4.1 s); 1,000 keys answered 200 per call (9.4 s).
carton: The host answers at most BLOB_HEADS_PER_REQUEST keys per call; the client asks again for the rest.

observed: Not hit: the vault stores 1 MiB chunks.

value: not a Cloudflare limit: a dead link keeps the WebSocket 'open'
observed: Old client: through a 5-minute outage the socket stayed open, status 'Syncing' for 5 min, 0 offline events; resumed only on TCP's retransmission timer (everything settled 66.5 s after the edits ended).
carton: Fixed (fix/cf-dead-link): the transport closes a link whose keepalive goes unanswered for 15 s, and pings on a send after silence.

value: not a Cloudflare limit: Workers Free's 100k requests/day across the account
observed: A client whose session the host refuses retried 86 times a minute (~0.57 s gaps), ~2 Worker requests per try: ~245k/day per stuck client, 2.5x the Free plan's daily requests.
carton: Fixed (fix/cf-reconnect-backoff): exponential backoff with jitter to 15 s, 5 min while the session is refused.

value: Workers 100k requests/day; DO 100k requests, 13,000 GB-s, 5M rows read, 100k rows written per day (Free)
observed: Not hit on purpose: hitting one would take the live showcase site down until 00:00 UTC (same account).
carton: Not measured. The lab's own daily write cap (fix/cf-write-cap) was shown instead: 429 DailyWriteCap with Retry-After and a clear message; the uploader stops resumably.

value: the lab deployments' own cap (fix/cf-write-cap): R2 8 GiB/day, no-R2 4 GiB/day, 20k write calls/day
observed: A 256 MB vault upload after the day's earlier uploads was refused: 429 DailyWriteCap.
carton: Refused before any byte is stored; the client backs off and stops resumably with the server's message.

value: not a Cloudflare limit: DO storage 5 GB (Free), $0.20/GB-month (Paid)
observed: The vault had no sweep for abandoned multipart uploads: a killed 1 GB upload left ~600 MB of parts in the DO for good (dropped by the lab).
carton: Fixed (fix/cf-vault-sweep, deployed to both lab Workers 02:14 UTC): an alarm deletes unfinished uploads untouched for 24 h, 500 rows a pass; not yet exercised live (24 h).

value: workerd cancels a request's work when its client disconnects, unless it is held with ctx.waitUntil (then up to 30 s more)
observed: An uploader killed mid-part: its part request ended 'canceled' in the tail before its finally ran, so the R2 adapter's part lock stayed held for LOCK_TTL_MS (30 min) and 5 resume sessions were refused 'PreconditionFailed: part 33 is being uploaded by another request' (2026-11-02). A 30 s link cut (no disconnect, TCP stalls) was not affected.
carton: Fixed (fix/cf-part-lock): the Worker hands each request's work to waitUntil; after the fix the killed part's request ran on 11.9 s, released its lock, and the upload resumed in one more session.

value: not a Cloudflare limit: Node's happy-eyeballs connect abandons each address after 250 ms (autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeout, Node 20+)
observed: On the bad profile (~400 ms round trip) every Node fetch, node:https request and WebSocket failed to connect (ETIMEDOUT / UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT); curl connected in 2.0-2.5 s; with the attempt time at 2 s or the selection off a put went through.
carton: Fixed (fix/cf-slow-link-connect): Carton's Node HTTP and WebSocket clients raise the default to at least 2 s; sync and uploads then work on bad.

value: DO rows written: 100k a day (Free); the vault writes ~4,070 per GB uploaded
observed: 3 of 3 vault uploads of 1 GiB wrote exactly 4,370 rows each (a row per MiB written as a part, copied on complete, the part rows deleted).
carton: Without R2, the Free plan's daily rows cap the account's vault uploads at about 24 GB a day (before any edits); the vault sweep adds a row per row it deletes.

observed: With several runs at once it kept 24-30% of a proxy run's 3,018 requests (no sampling notice printed); with one run at a time it was complete (1.00 per connect, 136 per GiB uploaded).
